strategy_rationale: The hidden test contains days 20-end of each month while training contains days 1-19. This is a sub_period_pattern with direction=train_lower (Priority 1). To mirror this gap, rows with day >= 14 (top ~32% of training days, i.e. days 14-19) are held out as validation, while days 1-13 are used for training. This faithfully simulates the model needing to extrapolate from early-month data to late-month periods, which is exactly the hidden evaluation structure. A naive chronological holdout would not respect the within-month split pattern and would give optimistically biased scores.
simulates_hidden_evaluation: Holdout rows are days 14-19 in each month (train file); the hidden test rows are days 20-end. Both are the latter portion of each month, so the model must learn from early-month patterns and generalise to late-month conditions — matching the real gap.

validation_limitations: Single holdout (not k-fold) so variance of the estimate is higher. The holdout does not capture temporal drift between years 2011 and 2012 (the model trains on all months within the 2-year span). Distribution shift in humidity and atemp between train and prediction may cause optimistic local scores. Sub-targets registered/casual are train-only so sub-target modeling must be validated carefully.
